Conflicting evidence! The permissions.html says "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." Hmm. Actually the well-known historical fact: the permission model DOES apply to workers (workers inherit). But this doc as fetched says it doesn't inherit. The task says: "If the sources do not establish one consistent worker-inheritance answer, state the limitation rather than silently choosing a convenient claim." So I must state the conflict as UNVERIFIED and suggest resolving via worker_threads docs for v24.21.0.

Passing an empty or modified execArgv to a worker does not grant it additional permissions." vs permissions.html constraint: "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." These directly conflict. I could fetch the worker_threads doc for v24.21.0. That would be a third source. I have 8 inference steps, used 2 (one call block counts as one step? That's a documented fact — env file outside read list is still loaded. That is fine for launcher trust, but means the read list isn't a complete inventory of file access.

- --allow-fs-read wildcard: "After passing a wildcard character (*) all subsequent characters will be ignored. For example: /home/*.js will work similar to /home/*." So --allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js actually permits /srv/jobs/* — everything in the directory, not just .js files. Also, "When the permission model is initialized, it will automatically add a wildcard (*) if the specified directory exists."
- Symlinks: "Symbolic links will be followed even to locations outside of the set of paths... Relative symbolic links may allow access to arbitrary files and directories." Customer-uploaded dirs may contain symlinks → arbitrary read.
- Existing file descriptors via node:fs bypass the permission model. Also drop() does not close/revoke already-open fds. Job gets an already-open fd → bypass/by-passes the model.
- process._debugProcess() cross-process inspector — not gated; operator must use OS-level isolation.
- node:sqlite, wasi etc.

SECURITY.md: threat model — trust the code it is asked to run, "The code run inherits all the privileges of the execution user." Permission model "designed to reduce the blast radius of mistakes in trusted application code, not to act as a security boundary against intentional misuse." So tenant isolation certification: No.
